findings.reason: without an open followup carrying the invocation, §28's declared measure is never run and the plan's remaining work is unbuildable from the plan itself.
findings.text: §28 is declared `implementable` but its adding commit `a8a514a1b` created the section without an open followup, so the plan's own chain never dispatches it: `f-tsigah-repair-wave-at-95ff28824` still recommends `/reckon-build the-suite-is-green-at-head §4` while §4 is declared `done`, and `f-tsigah-027` recommends §27, which is the only section the chain actually reaches — a coordinator following the followups builds §27 and stops, leaving §28 `implementable` and undispatched; the same author's §27 commit (`f506fdf20`) added both the section and its followup `f-tsigah-027`, so the omission is specific to §28

findings.reason: the figures are true and the evidence sits in the run directory the section already names, so a reader can reach it; naming the file is a one-line correction that changes no work.
findings.text: §28's central measurement, "Repeated six times per tree in one window, base passed 0 of 6 and head 1 of 6", cites no path: the two logs it names are single whole-file runs of `tests/test_removed_flag_migration.py` (each `1 failed, N passed`), and the six-run arms it relies on to refute the dispatch-change attribution are recorded only in an unnamed sibling file in the same run directory (`diag-stability.log`: `ARM head … passed 1, failed 5` at line 416, `ARM base … passed 0, failed 6` at line 909)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §28's per-tree arm figures are uncited (see FINDING).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §28's done-when is measurable (ten consecutive passes at head under a named parallel load, with the load command and sampled load average recorded) and it declares a negative control whose red log is required.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §28's gate and its cited failing-run evidence sit under `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<run>/`, both of which exist and survive the run.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §28 introduces no new symbol and carries no version tag, ticket number or changelog prose into the test file it names.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause (a 1.5 s ceiling on a poll that already returns early) matches the cited evidence: `gate-final-base.log` and `gate-final-head.log` in run `r-20261019T212943222385-a-dispatch-yields-to-its-sessions-older-request` each show the one failure, and the same run's arms record `ARM base: passed 0, failed 6` against `ARM head: passed 1, failed 5` (load average 22.51), so the failure reproduces at the base revision without the dispatch change; `_wait_for_the_first_delivery` (`tests/test_removed_flag_migration.py:127`) is called with `bound=1.5` at line 291 and the failing assertion at line 299 is `assert rows`, the empty-stdout case the section names.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §28 carries one deliverable, the test's follower-wait ceiling, confined to one write path.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §28 is declared `implementable` (docs/plans/the-suite-is-green-at-head.html:743) but no open followup invokes it: the only open followups are `f-tsigah-repair-wave-at-95ff28824` (prompt `/reckon-build the-suite-is-green-at-head §4`, and §4 is `done`) and `f-tsigah-027` (`§27`).
